articles.title: I built a period tracker that never asks for an account
articles.excerpt: This week I shipped the first public version of Mori, an Android period tracker. The product rule I started with was simple: no account, ever, for the core features. Period data is some of the most se…
articles.body: This week I shipped the first public version of Mori, an Android period tracker. The product rule I started with was simple: no account, ever, for the core features. Why that rule Period data is some of the most sensitive stuff on a phone. In most tracker apps it ends up on a company server, attached to an email, behind a login the app demands before it even opens. That model has real-world consequences — after Roe v. Wade fell, the White House literally warned people about period tracker apps because server-side reproductive data can be subpoenaed. So I built the opposite default: records live in a local SQLite database on the phone. Without cloud sync, nothing ever leaves the device. There is no signup screen.
articles.author: Alfred Chaos

articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 1: Touch Grass . What I Built PocketTrail turns a short activity request into a pocket-sized plan for a nearby green place. It is a new prototype built during Week 1 with Codex. Its purpose is small: choose an activity, find a place that leaves time for the return trip, save a card, then leave the screen. The starting pack covers three Paris parks. The starting coordinates are an example, not a detected or claimed personal location. People elsewhere can replace the park pack with places they know and source links. Demo Try PocketTrail . A calm activity and a 90-minute budget produced Jardin des Tuileries with approximately 36 minutes each way and 18 minutes outside.

articles.title: TASK#STOMP: A Windows Backdoor That Lives in Scheduled Tasks and VBS
articles.excerpt: TASK#STOMP: A Windows Backdoor That Lives in Scheduled Tasks and VBS Securonix published an analysis of TASK#STOMP, a Windows backdoor that uses only components already present on the host. The payloa…
articles.body: TASK#STOMP: A Windows Backdoor That Lives in Scheduled Tasks and VBS Securonix published an analysis of TASK#STOMP, a Windows backdoor that uses only components already present on the host. The payload is PowerShell, persistence comes from scheduled tasks and the Startup folder, and collection targets documents, clipboard contents, screenshots and saved Wi-Fi passwords. The design goal is long-term espionage rather than immediate disruption. The infection chain The observed chain begins with a randomly named VBS file in a user-writable path, for example 95c9050t66.vbs . Securonix has not confirmed how it arrives, and the available evidence cannot separate phishing, a browser download, removable media, remote access or archive extraction.
articles.author: kozhevniko

articles.excerpt: How to Write a Freelance Proposal That Wins the Project (Step-by-Step) You found a promising lead. You had a good call. Now you need to send a proposal — and this is where many freelancers either free…
articles.body: How to Write a Freelance Proposal That Wins the Project (Step-by-Step) You found a promising lead. You had a good call. Now you need to send a proposal — and this is where many freelancers either freeze or spend three days polishing a document that never gets signed. The truth: clients don't hire the most beautiful proposal. They hire the one that makes the decision easy. A good proposal answers three questions fast: What exactly will I get? What does it cost? What happens next? This guide walks you through how to write a freelance proposal step by step, with concrete structure, examples, and a checklist you can reuse for every project. Step 1: Start With the Client's Words, Not Your Bio Most proposals open with "About me" and a list of tools. That's backwards.

articles.body: Как составить proposal for freelancers, который закрывает сделку, а не лежит в папке «Отправлено» Если вы фрилансер, знакомо это чувство: лид тёплый, вы обсудили задачу, клиент говорит «звучит отлично, пришлите коммерческое». Вы садитесь вечером писать предложение, тратите три часа, отправляете — и тишина. Через неделю узнаёте, что клиент ушёл к другому подрядчику, который просто ответил быстрее и понятнее. Проблема почти никогда не в цене. Проблема в том, что proposal for freelancers часто пишется как эссе о вашей крутости, а не как документ, который помогает клиенту принять решение. Ниже — разбор структуры, конкретные формулировки и чек-лист, который можно применить к следующему проекту уже сегодня. Почему большинство предложений не срабатывают Три типичные ошибки: Слишком долго.

articles.title: Taming the FFmpeg Stampede: Writing a Custom eBPF Scheduler with Linux 6.12 sched_ext
articles.excerpt: Have you ever launched 20–30 concurrent ffmpeg encoding jobs on a beefy multi-core server, only to watch the entire system grind to a halt? Even on modern NVMe drives and 64-thread machines, running d…
articles.body: Have you ever launched 20–30 concurrent ffmpeg encoding jobs on a beefy multi-core server, only to watch the entire system grind to a halt? Even on modern NVMe drives and 64-thread machines, running dozens of heavy video encoders simultaneously can trigger the dreaded I/O convoy effect . The standard Linux scheduler (EEVDF) tries to be fair by giving everyone CPU time at once. The result? All 25 processes decompress, encode, and flush buffers to disk at the exact same moment—saturating memory channels, dirtying page cache pages, and freezing interactive tasks. With Linux 6.12 , we finally have an elegant way to solve this at the kernel level without recompiling the kernel: sched_ext (SCX) , the extensible BPF scheduler class.
articles.author: Pawel Suchanecki

articles.excerpt: An engrossing expansion full of interesting new characters and vibrant enemies.
articles.body: The first Dark Arisen expansion for the original Dragon’s Dogma has a well-lauded place in video game history as the expansion that “fixed” the base game, sanding down the rough technical edges and tweaking things to make the notoriously obtuse RPG more approachable. It also added hours of new content, spiraling an already heady story directly into the heavens on the back of dragon wings. Dark Arisen 2 isn’t as transformational as the first one was, primarily because many of Dragon’s Dogma 2’s biggest issues have been fixed through incremental patching since it came out in 2024. But the new content here definitely flies in the same ambitious skies as its predecessor, pushing the story and world design to new heights, even if some of the new progression options get left behind.

articles.excerpt: A visualization of a dark Moon eclipsing the Sun is marked with handwritten notes in this April 6, 2026, screenshot from an Artemis II crew member’s tablet. NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman (in blue) and…
articles.body: NASA A visualization of a dark Moon eclipsing the Sun is marked with handwritten notes in this April 6, 2026, screenshot from an Artemis II crew member’s tablet. NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman (in blue) and Victor “Ike” Glover (in green) and CSA (Canadian Space Agency) Jeremy Hansen (in red) observed impact flashes and their locations, which are noted on the image. Overall, the astronauts reported seeing five extremely faint “pinprick” bursts of light from their view aboard Orion, which was 46,000 miles away from the Moon at the time. These flashes are sparked by rocky fragments hitting the Moon.
